text:
Sean Kuraly returned to the lineup Tuesday against Los Angeles after missing the Bruins' previous three games, and walked into a 3-0 loss, Boston's third straight. The 33-year-old, in his second stint with the club after 270 games in his first, has played only seven of Boston's 21 games and has no points yet.

The empty line hides something. When Kuraly is on the ice at five on five, Boston has 68.2% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, about 15 points better than without him. In seven games that number is mostly noise, but it points to a fourth-line center doing the dull parts right. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of high-value passes last season (across the slot or from behind the net), while his line dumps the puck in more than it carries.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year, which is the honest frame. For a team that has lost three in a row and scored four goals in that stretch, a checker who tilts the ice is welcome. The goals will need to come from someone else.
